title: Studio sample catalog
brief:
Complete the following real project in the current, initially empty directory. Choose the deliverables, media, tools, structure and implementation that serve the intended user. Build usable artifacts and check your work. Deliver the project itself. Omit personally identifying credits, author signatures and model or toolchain identity labels. No network access or credentials are provided.

Design and build an offline sample catalog for a small upholstery studio. Three staff members use a shared laptop to find fabric swatches and track which ones are out with clients. Each record needs a sample code, color family, fabric type, drawer location, and checkout status. The physical cabinet has drawers A through F, and existing paper tags use codes such as C-014. Include enough fictional sample records to demonstrate searching and filtering. Staff should be able to correct records and export a copy of their data. Starting from an empty directory, choose the technologies, deliverables, and file layout. Favor a workflow that works with keyboard entry at the counter.

files.name: README.md
files.body:
# Selvedge · Upholstery sample catalog

Keep the project folder together and open **index.html** in a desktop browser. The catalog works offline with no install or sign-in. On first use, it starts with 18 fictional samples, including five client loans. The fabric illustrations represent color and weave.

## At the counter

- Press **/** to search. Type a tag such as **C-014**, a swatch name, or a client. **Enter** opens the first match. **Down Arrow** moves focus to the first result.
- Combine drawer, color, and fabric filters. Select **With clients** to find outstanding loans. Grid and list views show the same records.
- Open a sample and select **Check out**. Enter the client or project and press **Enter**. When it comes back, open the record and select **Return to studio**. File it in the drawer shown.
- Select **Edit record** to correct a tag, drawer, fabric, color, name, or borrower. The drawer can change independently of the paper tag.
- Press **N** outside a field to add a sample. Each code uses A–F, a hyphen, and three digits. **Tab** moves between controls, and **Esc** closes the record without saving pending form edits.

## Shared laptop and copies

All three staff should open the same file at the same path in the same regular browser profile. The browser stores saved records locally. Private browsing, clearing browser data, switching profiles, or moving the file can remove access to that copy.

**Export CSV** downloads the entire catalog, including borrower names, even when the view is filtered. Save dated copies somewhere the studio can find them. The CSV opens in spreadsheet software. Changes made in a spreadsheet stay in the exported copy.

files.name: README.md
files.body:
# Selvedge Studio · Swatch catalog

Open **index.html** in a regular Chrome window on the shared laptop. Keep the project files together and use the same browser profile and file location for all three staff members. The catalog runs offline and opens with 24 fictional swatches across drawers A–F.

## At the counter

- Press **/** to search. Type a paper tag such as `C-014` or `c014`, a color, a fabric, or a client or project reference. Press **Enter** to open an exact code or the only matching result.
- Use the color, fabric, drawer, and status filters together. The three totals above the inventory also set the status filter. Tab to the drawer choices and use the arrow keys to change drawers.
- Open **Edit** to correct a record. To send a swatch out, select **Checked out** and optionally enter a client or project reference. On return, select **In cabinet** and save. Returning a swatch clears its checkout reference. The drawer field tracks where the swatch belongs.
- Press **N** outside a text field to add a swatch. Codes are unique and saved in uppercase. A new code beginning with A–F and a hyphen suggests a drawer when the drawer field is empty. Press **Esc** to close a dialog.

## Keep a copy

Changes are saved in the current browser profile. Use **Export data** to save a spreadsheet copy (**CSV**) or a restorable catalog backup (**JSON**). Both exports contain every record, regardless of filters.

To replace the fictional records with your own, choose **Export data → Start a blank catalog** and confirm. To recover the catalog after clearing browser data, or to move it to another folder or laptop, open the catalog at the destination, choose **Export data → Restore from a backup**, select your JSON file, and confirm the replacement.
